title: Battle of the River Plate
subtitle: South Atlantic · 1–20 December 1939
footnote: Times as in Commodore Harwood's despatch (Zone +2, i.e. UTC−2, one hour ahead of Montevideo). The squadron's 05:20 position, Graf Spee's victims and the wreck position are from the despatch and Wikipedia; Graf Spee's own track and the Altmark's whereabouts are reconstructed. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

forceg.name: RN Force G — South America Division (Harwood)

spee: Disguised with a dummy funnel and turret, hunting the Cape route
Sinks the Blue Star liner Doric Star (10,086 GRT) — 19°15′S 5°05′E; her RRR signal reaches Harwood
Sinks Tairoa 170 miles to the south-west
Last rendezvous with Altmark; 140 prisoners transferred
Sinks Streonshalh; her secret route papers point Langsdorff at the Plate traffic
The Arado breaks down; disguise removed
Sights masts; identifies Exeter and two destroyers — then cruisers. Opens fire at 06:18
Turns 150° to port under smoke; Exeter's B turret already gone
Hard to port toward Ajax and Achilles; hit amidships
Steadies on 270°, then 255° at 22 knots — for Montevideo
Shadowed at 15 miles by Achilles and Ajax
Two salvoes at Ajax at 26,000 yards
Fires at Achilles off Punta Negra after sunset
Weighs with a skeleton crew; 700 men have gone to the Tacoma
'GRAF SPEE has blown herself up' — Ajax's aircraft. Wreck at 34°58′S 56°18′W
altmark: Loiters in the South Atlantic until 24 January; intercepted by Cossack in Jøssingfjord 16 February
forceg: Ajax off the Plate; Achilles off Rio, Exeter at Port Stanley, Cumberland off the Plate
Doric Star's signal: Harwood works out that a raider steaming at 15 knots can reach the Plate on 13 December
Exeter joins from the Falklands; Harwood signals his battle plan
34°34′S 49°17′W, course 060°, 14 knots — Ajax, Achilles, Exeter in line
Smoke bearing 320°; Exeter: 'I think it is a pocket battleship'
First Division closes to draw fire from Exeter
Ajax fires four torpedoes at 9,000 yards; X and Y turrets disabled a minute later
Ajax and Achilles break off east under smoke — 'a serious shortage of ammunition'
Shadowing at 15 miles, Achilles to starboard, Ajax to port
Off Montevideo; Cumberland ordered up from the Falklands
Patrol off English Bank; Ajax oils from Olynthus
Watching the scuttling from the estuary
cumberland: Sails on Captain Fallowfield's own initiative
1,014 miles in 34 hours; takes Exeter's place off the Plate
doricstar: Blue Star liner from Auckland with frozen meat and wool
Stopped and sunk after transmitting RRR

spee.name: Kapitän zur See Hans Langsdorff
spee.bio: A Jutland veteran who sank nine ships totalling 50,000 tons without taking a single merchant life. Wounded twice on his open bridge on 13 December, he ran for Montevideo rather than fight on with his fuel system damaged, then, refused time for repairs and believing a battle squadron waited outside, scuttled his ship to save his crew.
spee.fate: Shot himself in Buenos Aires on 20 December 1939, aged 45.

forceg.name: Commodore Henry Harwood
forceg.bio: Guessed from Doric Star's distress call that the raider would come to the Plate, and had his three cruisers waiting. His plan — attack immediately in two divisions from either flank — had been worked out at the War College years before. Promoted rear-admiral and knighted the same day.

cumberland.name: Captain W. H. G. Fallowfield
cumberland.bio: Sailed from Port Stanley at noon on his own initiative, before Harwood's signal reached him, and covered 1,014 miles in 34 hours to replace the crippled Exeter off Montevideo.

ships.name: Admiral Graf Spee
ships.sunkBy: Scuttled by her own crew off Montevideo
damage: Some seventy hits; galley and fuel system damaged

ships.name: HMS Exeter
extra: All three turrets out, 61 dead, 7° list — hauls off south-east at 18 knots
Emergency repairs at Port Stanley; a 13-month refit at Devonport follows

strikes.name: Ajax's Seafox spots for the squadron
strikes.note: Lt Lewin's Seafox is catapulted under fire and spots for Ajax and Achilles until the break-off

torpedoes.note: Starboard tubes; Graf Spee combs the tracks
Fired at 9,000 yards as the range closes — all miss

engagements.note: Six 11-inch guns concentrate on Exeter, then shift to the light cruisers
Eight 8-inch until B, then A, then Y turret are knocked out
Sixteen 6-inch guns; some 70 hits are claimed on Graf Spee
Two salvoes at Ajax at 26,000 yards
Fires at Achilles off Punta Negra

events: Doric Star sunk — her RRR signal tells Harwood a raider is loose on the Cape route
Tairoa sunk 170 miles south-west of Doric Star
Harwood's appreciation: the raider will reach the Plate on 13 December — Ajax, Achilles and Exeter to concentrate there
Streonshalh sunk; her papers send Langsdorff to the Plate
Ajax and Achilles meet at 35°S 50°W
Exeter joins; Harwood's plan — attack at once, by day or night, in two divisions
Smoke bearing 320°: Exeter sent to investigate
Graf Spee opens fire at 19,000 yards
Exeter's B turret wrecked; bridge swept, Captain Bell wounded
Achilles' director hit — four killed
Ajax's X and Y turrets disabled by one shell
Break-off: Harwood turns east under smoke; Graf Spee heads west for the Plate
Cumberland ordered up from the Falklands
Exeter ordered to the Falklands
Graf Spee anchors at Montevideo
Cumberland arrives off the Plate
Uruguay grants 72 hours; British merchantmen sail to invoke the 24-hour rule; the Admiralty hints Ark Royal and Renown are near
Over 700 of Graf Spee's crew transfer to the German freighter Tacoma
Graf Spee blown up by her own crew in the estuary
Langsdorff shoots himself in Buenos Aires, lying on his ship's ensign

ports.name: Montevideo
ports.note: Neutral Uruguay; Graf Spee's 72-hour refuge. Her dead lie in the Cementerio del Norte

ports.name: Buenos Aires
ports.note: Neutral Argentina; Graf Spee's crew interned here, Langsdorff buried at La Chacarita

ports.name: Port Stanley
ports.note: Falklands base: Cumberland refitting, Exeter's refuge after the battle

ports.name: Rio de Janeiro
ports.note: Achilles' patrol area before the concentration

ports.name: Samborombón Bay
ports.note: RFA Olynthus oils the cruisers here and off the Rouen Bank

ports.name: London — Admiralty
ports.note: Feeds the newspapers with Renown and Ark Royal 'off the Plate' — they were five days away

ports.name: Berlin — Seekriegsleitung
ports.note: Raeder and Hitler leave Langsdorff the choice: fight through to Buenos Aires or scuttle — but no internment
